key_insight: Detonation-sprayed self-fluxing Ni–Cr–Fe–B–Si–C coatings can be tuned from low-friction to high-wear-resistance behavior by adjusting barrel fill, gas ratio, and inter-shot delay.
engineering_relevance: The study provides process windows for restoring and strengthening machine parts with coatings that balance hardness, porosity, surface roughness, and tribological performance.
method: Changed inter-shot delay from 0 to 1 s and compared coating microstructure, hardness, roughness, friction, and wear.
evidence_signal: At 48% barrel fill and O/C = 1.026 the coating reached the lowest friction (μ = 0.674 ± 0.136), while O/C = 1.856 with up to 1 s delay gave the best wear resistance (specific wear rate = 0.000189 mm³/(N·m)) and Ra dropped from 5.00 to 3.60 μm with longer delay.
watch_item: Optimizing for low friction can increase wear, so parameter selection requires a trade-off and may not transfer directly without matching spray equipment and part geometry.
paper_title: Development of a Method for Producing Self-Fluxing Nickel-Based Coatings by Detonation Spraying
